claims.text: Spark plasma sintering is effective for achieving large-scale reaction in RHEA-Cu composite structures.
Spark plasma sintering is effective for producing a stable microstructure in RHEA-Cu composite structures.
There is a significant positive heat of mixing between the RHEA components and Cu.
SPS rapidly heats and consolidates a powder mixture containing refractory-element and copper powders.
High heating rates, elevated temperatures, controlled pressure, and an inert atmosphere are typical SPS processing conditions.
SPS causes rapid densification of the RHEA-Cu powder mixture.
SPS enhances transient diffusion at interfaces between RHEA particles and Cu.
Rapid densification and enhanced transient interfacial diffusion mitigate the effects of unfavorable mixing enthalpy.
SPS provides rapid thermal activation and consolidation.
Rapid SPS processing limits prolonged high-temperature exposure.
Prolonged high-temperature exposure exacerbates phase segregation in RHEA-Cu composites.
The high heating rate of SPS promotes a controlled interfacial reaction.
A controlled interfacial reaction produces a stable composite microstructure.
SPS processing will produce a homogeneous distribution of RHEA and copper phases.
The SPS-processed RHEA-Cu composite will have improved mechanical strength.
The SPS-processed RHEA-Cu composite will have improved irradiation resistance.
The SPS-processed RHEA-Cu composite will have improved thermal stability.
Conventional sintering or melting often produces phase segregation or unstable microstructures in RHEA-Cu systems.
The inferior microstructures attributed to conventional processing result from extended high-temperature exposure and the large positive heat of mixing.
The proposed effect applies under optimized SPS conditions and may depend strongly on powder characteristics and processing route.
